g.title: kind.nsp: A named resolution scope when a more specific kind is not yet chosen.
kind.prj: A collaborative or platform organization scope, separate from team ownership.
kind.dir: A path or name grouping; not automatically a security or storage boundary.
kind.reg: A catalog of agreed definitions, domains, bindings or contracts.
kind.cld: A declared cloud hosting scope; managed status is a separate property.
kind.acc: An administrative cloud resource scope with explicit owner and policy.
kind.rgn: A declared geographical or regional placement scope.
kind.az: A declared failure or availability boundary whose guarantees need metadata.
kind.site: An on-premises or other site scope, distinct from a software namespace.
kind.net: A connectivity or network-scope boundary; not inferred from drawing overlap.
kind.clu: A coordinated group of service or compute instances.
kind.srv: A deployed service endpoint hosting or exposing resources.
kind.host: A compute placement instance, not a database schema.
kind.ctr: A runtime placement instance with its orchestration context declared.
kind.vol: A physical or logical storage-allocation resource with platform scope.
kind.dev: A local data-producing or data-storing device.
kind.env: Development, test, staging, production or another explicitly named scope.
kind.secz: A security scope requiring explicit policy; not implied by location.
kind.prl: A logical fragmentation policy with its key, method and version.
kind.par: A logical subset of a dataset; not inherently a deployment unit.
kind.shd: A distribution fragment identified separately from its deployed copies.
kind.plc: An assignment of a resource or copy to an infrastructure scope.
kind.rpl: A distinct deployed copy linked to the represented logical data and source.
kind.rps: A group of coordinated copies with explicit role and consistency policy.
